speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Meningococcemia. Based on the rapid onset of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating without focal neurological deficits, this presentation is highly suggestive of a severe bacterial infection with potential meningeal involvement. Immediate empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluid resuscitation are critical.
